focus: KeepInjuryFractions and the SettingsChanged/TraitsChanged health handling
diffSource: since build 57 (2026-10-10T03:38:54Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: KeepInjuryFractions only scales down, so a down-then-up round trip heals injuries for free
findings.detail: The early return `if (newFactor >= oldFactor ...) return;` means injuries shrink when the factor falls but stay the same in absolute hit points when it rises. Two paths reach this in normal play: lowering the health-per-point slider and then raising it again (each window close runs WriteSettings, which calls SettingsChanged on every titan), or a trait being removed and then re-added (RemoveTraitInternal/AddTraitInternal both go through TraitsChanged). Either way, part of every injury is permanently healed. To keep fractions both ways, drop the `newFactor >= oldFactor` half of the guard and keep only `oldFactor <= 0f`. If you do, loop over a copy of the hediff list: when an injury's severity goes up, the Severity setter calls Notify_HediffChanged once the rounded value changes (Hediff.cs:239-269), and the list is being enumerated at that point.

findings.title: Slider changes made outside the loaded game never rescale saved injuries
findings.detail: WriteSettings returns early when Current.Game is null, and only reaches pawns in the loaded game. healthFactor is [Unsaved], so on load it is recalculated from the current setting. A save written under a higher healthPerPoint therefore loads with injuries sized for the old, larger health pool. Parts can be at or below 0 HP and the injury total can be past the lethal threshold, so the titan dies on its next Notify_HediffChanged. That is the exact failure this change fixes for in-game slider changes. One fix: save the last applied factor with Scribe_Values and call KeepInjuryFractions with it at PostLoadInit.

findings.title: TraitsChanged takes the old factor from the cache, which can be stale or missing
findings.detail: `oldHealth = healthBuiltFor != null ? healthFactor : 1f` reads the cached field because the trait list has already changed by the time TraitsChanged runs (AddTraitInternal line 180, RemoveTraitInternal line 191). If no HealthFactor read has happened yet (healthBuiltFor null, e.g. just after load, since it is [Unsaved]), it assumes 1.0. A titan whose real factor was above 1 would then have its injuries scaled too little or not at all. If cachedStage was rebuilt by Diet or CurStage without HealthFactor being read, the cached value describes an older trait set. Reading HealthFactor in Add/RemoveTraitInternal before the list changes and passing it in would give the exact old value. In practice HealthScale is read constantly, so the window is small.

findings.title: Per-trait clamp to 0.25 changes balance for content-mod traits and is undocumented
findings.detail: TraitFactor now floors each trait at MinFactor, after multiplying in healthScaleFactor. A content mod that sets healthScaleFactor below 0.25 (e.g. 0.1) now gets 0.25, and the combinations it appears in get tougher than before (a 0.1 drawback with a ×2 bonus was 0.25 overall, now 0.5). For a single trait the result is unchanged, because Factor() already applied the same floor. The class summary formula (TitanHealth.cs:11) and the healthScaleFactor doc (TitanTraitDef.cs:66-69) don't mention the floor, so content authors won't know.

findings.title: Live hediff list is enumerated while Severity is set
findings.detail: Lowering an injury's severity only calls Notify_HediffChanged if its stage index changes (Hediff.cs:239-269). Vanilla injury defs are stageless, so this is safe today. A modded staged Hediff_Injury could still trigger CheckForStateChange in the middle of the foreach. Looping over a copy (`.ToList()`, as Notify_TraitDiscovered already does) removes the risk for little cost.

checked: Patch_Pawn_HealthScale postfix still binds to the Pawn.HealthScale getter (verify_patches: 1 of 1 resolved)
No corpus mod patches Pawn.get_HealthScale, so there is no prefix/transpiler conflict
SettingsChanged reads HealthFactor before marking the stage dirty, so in the normal case the old factor comes from the still-valid cache and the new one reflects the new setting
SettingsChanged is called once from WriteSettings (window close), not every frame while the slider is dragged (Mod.cs:25-28)
Hediff.Severity setter: lowering a stageless injury's severity does not call Notify_HediffChanged, and scale > 0 keeps severity above 0, so the foreach does not modify the list in vanilla
KeepInjuryFractions runs before Notify_HediffChanged in both callers and only when the hediff is in the set, so pawn.health.hediffSet is non-null there
Hediff_MissingPart is not a Hediff_Injury, so missing parts are not scaled
Lint rules prefix-returns-void, defof-in-mod-ctor, patch-success-always: none apply to the changed code
